children: shares dropped nearly 6.2% at 10.35 a.m. ET on November 16 in regular trading, extending Friday's slide. TipRanks tied the pressure to Nvidia's leadership change, noting investor worry that Nvidia could fund neocloud firms less aggressively. CoreWeave has a $6.3 billion capacity deal with Nvidia and received a $2 billion equity purchase from it, according to the same report.

The latest quarter shows both scale and strain. CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, up about 168%, and a backlog of about $132.5 billion. It raised 2026 revenue guidance to $13.0 billion to $13.3 billion. The cost side moved too: net loss widened to $709 million, net interest expense reached $846 million, and the company expects $1.05 billion to $1.15 billion of interest in the fourth quarter. Capex guidance runs $37 billion to $39 billion this year.

Third-quarter interest was about 2.2 times adjusted operating income of $379 million, so growth is still being funded with expensive capital. The backlog equals nearly five times the $27.4 billion market cap, which shows how much revenue the market is discounting for financing risk. GuruFocus gives CoreWeave a GF Score of just 14/100, flagging weak profitability and a stretched balance sheet. GuruFocus publishes no GF Value for the company. Nvidia's November 17 call is the immediate test, especially any comment on customer financing arrangements.

title: CoreWeave Stocks Drop 3.95% as Nvidia Leadership Shake-Up Rattles Neocloud Lenders
